title: ms-swift 4.6.0 deploy media path reads arbitrary host files by default

root_cause.note: swift deploy accepts image/audio/video fields from chat requests. `to_base64` checks the local path with SafeMediaPath and then opens it, but SafeMediaPath returns the path unchanged when SWIFT_MEDIA_ALLOWED_DIRS is unset (the default). A caller can therefore name any host file; its bytes are inlined into the request and can be read back through the model or error behavior. The 4.6.0 guard is opt-in, so the default deployment remains an arbitrary-file-read primitive.

preconditions: attacker can send a chat/completion request with a local media path
steps: extract the verbatim upstream SafeMediaPath class and MultiModalRequestMixin.to_base64 function
call to_base64 with a canary file path outside any allowed directory
decode the returned base64 and verify the canary content; then set SWIFT_MEDIA_ALLOWED_DIRS to an empty dir and observe the refusal
expected_evidence: base64 returned by the upstream function decodes to the canary marker
with the allowlist set, SafeMediaPath raises ValueError
cleanup: canary files under evidence/ are rewritten per run
notes: Function-level reproduction of the real 4.6.0 guard + inlining path; the FastAPI server/model are not started because the host has no GPU. The default-unsafe branch and the explicit allowlist branch are both the upstream code.
